steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Lisburn, that shameless bastard. Calls us over to help out with herding this lot, and now him and his lady friend are nowhere to be found.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: He isn't actually thinking of settling down in Kjerag, is he? What d'you think?

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Weren't you the one egging him on the hardest earlier?

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: And now you're fussing over him actually going through with it?

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Just worried someone's trying to pull a fast one on him.

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Kjerag's folk are an honest lot, and if anything shady were happening, it would be us trying to fool them. You think they're swindling Lisburn? Save it. You're just jealous.

spans.text: Kjerag's folk are an honest lot, and if anything shady were happening, it would be
. You think they're swindling Lisburn? Save it. You're just jealous.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: You can't say that! We're soldiers! Protecting our country's our duty, and 'falling in love' must be the result of some kind of... subversive action!

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Hope you've got the energy to keep yelling like that during your next report.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Hope you've got the barefaced cheek to talk like that during your next report.

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Just shut up and get back to herding already.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Hey, I'd take being a herdsman my whole life over getting sent back to the battlefield.

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: As if that'll happen any time soon.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Don't be so sure about that. The boss got a letter from the Duke a few days ago. I dunno what's it about, but he's been murmuring to himself since he got it.

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Murmuring about what?

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: 'Rhodes Island'.

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Really? Only thing I've seen him worrying about lately is his prize burdenbeast. Like—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ohoho, what a good girl! Relax, relax.

steps.name: Docile Burdenbeast
steps.text: (Feeble cry)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Right, that's it, girl. Won't hurt a bit.

steps.name: Docile Burdenbeast
steps.text: (Pained cry)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now now, Lanny, stay calm, don't be afraid—
The burdenbeast in pain moves two steps towards Harold. He attempts to dodge out of the way while calming her down, but finds himself a step too slow.
'Cr-ack'.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Uh-oh.
He looks down to see his prosthetic leg in pieces.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Hahaha!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Jack.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Haha... Sorry, boss. I know you're going to send me off to the hospital, so at least let me get my laughs in now while I still can?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I am going to send you off, but not to the hospital.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I looked into it when we first arrived. The local hospitals can't help me repair this peg-leg of mine.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Then where do I need to go?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm afraid Rhodes Island's the only place that can fix this.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Rhodes Island, huh...? I thought there's a bit of bad blood between us, though.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: That is precisely why you must go.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This is your last chance to not have to head back into battle, and mine to not have to go back home and deal with nobles.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Seriously? I'll be off right away then, sir!

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: We've asked Engineering to have a look at your prosthetic, Mr. Craigavon.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Its inner structure was already on the verge of collapse before it got stepped on. Otherwise it wouldn't have broken with the weight of a burdenbeast.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Makes sense. It's been carrying a weight a hundred times greater than any burdenbeast, after all.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: So, what's the verdict from the experts?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I've got good news and bad news.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Good news first, if you would.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: The good news is that Rhodes Island has just obtained some new equipment that will allow us to repair your prosthetic.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Let me guess, the bad news is that you don't have the material to do it?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: No, our agreement with Karlan Trade covers the purchase of the material.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Then... Lack of manpower?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I'm afraid so. The technology in your prosthetic is rather advanced, and none of our operators currently in Kjerag have the technical know-how.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What a pity.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh* After so many years enjoying its retirement, it seems I must put my cane back to its original use.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: We do have someone from Engineering currently traveling Kjerag.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: She's on holiday, though, and she hasn't been in touch with our office since she arrived, so we're not entirely sure what her itinerary looks like.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: If we can find her, she might be able to help you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A hunt it is, then. I'll do it. Got any leads for me?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Hmm... Courier mentioned passing some goods over to her friends. He might know something.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Courier, that would be Weiss...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This puts me in a bit of a pickle.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: If it's not convenient for you—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: No, I'll go.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But your leg—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Not to worry. I am rather accustomed to walking with my cane. It's been my firm friend for about as long as that metal leg has.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I told him, as per your request, Mr. SilverAsh. He really did go off by himself. Is that everything, then?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Yes. I've discussed it with the Doctor.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Since he wants to use this opportunity to get closer to Rhodes Island, why, we are merely riding his coattails.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: He will not be ignorant of this.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The rest is all up to him.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Oh, I see you've come again today, Mr. Weiss.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Yep. I'll be following Sir Enciodes to Rhodes Island soon, so I decided to help out here a bit more often before I'm off.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Oh, that's wonderful to hear!

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Ah, right, there's an elderly gentleman who's been waiting for you for quite a while now.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: An elderly gentleman?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Long time no see, Mr. Weiss.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: It's been quite some time, Lord Viscount.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: I thought you would have left Kjerag by now.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, you are such a jocular young fellow, Weiss. Surely my every movement is under your watchful eye, no?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: You know that my master has long since called off surveillance on you.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: I'm happy for the free time myself. At least I don't have to worry about getting knocked silly.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You're a very straightforward young man. I must say, I much prefer dealing with people like you.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: So, why do you need me, all of a sudden?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Well, you see, I'm currently looking for one of Rhodes Island's master engineers to see if she can help repair my prosthetic.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I've heard you know where she's gone off to.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: I think I know who you're talking about.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I know, I know, it won't be so easy for me to get information out of you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I've talked it over with the staff here. How about I help you send your letters once my leg's all fixed up, hmm?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Forgive me. I cannot give out information regarding a Rhodes Island operator to a Victorian officer so lightly.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Bah, figured it wouldn't be quite so easy.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm afraid I'll have to ask Jack and the other lads to run around looking for her.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh* No, that won't work. They'll just lead to a misunderstanding.

steps.name: Harold & Depressed Passerby
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh? What's going on here, young lady?

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: *sigh*... It's nothing, just that the stress of work's too much for me.

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: I don't think I can take much more of it, but I can't afford to lose this job, either.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm afraid there's much in life out of our control, madam.

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: Today's a rare day off for me, but I don't feel happy. Even on vacation, all I can do is sit here like some kind of fool.

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: What joy is there in a life like this?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Young lady, would you happen to be interested in dance?

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: Somewhat, I guess.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Then, how about admiring a disabled old fogey dancing a jig?

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: Huh? But... your leg...?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Who said you can't dance with one leg, eh?
Harold says no more. With his cane in hand, he steps in front of the young woman, giving her a bow befitting a gentleman.

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: Huh?
As she gasps in surprise, Harold begins to dance, waving his cane this way and that.
First, he revolves around it, his foot moving with grace and aplomb.
His cane and his leather shoe rap against the ground, their rhythm a perfect match with the music being played in the nearby stores.

But the best has yet to come. As the music reaches its crescendo, he flings his cane into the air. It spins, spins, spins, before he deftly catches it like the most graceful of acrobats, all as the woman claps and cheers.
It seems she too has caught the dance bug as she joins him, and together they dance merrily on the street.
Passersby are unwittingly drawn in by Harold's magnetic energy. Some are happy to stand on the sidelines and applaud, while others join in with gusto.
The plaza has found itself the epicenter of festivity.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Better to join in and look a fool than sit out and be a bore, as I always say!

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: You're right!
As the music slowly draws to a close, Harold intends to use one last beautiful toss of his cane to serve as his curtain call.
But—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Now? Of all times?)
Perhaps it's due to lack of practice, or perhaps the lively atmosphere got to his head, but at the very last second, his hand slips.
The cane traces a beautiful arc in the air, but its destination is far from his reach.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Uh-oh.
As if refusing to let the show end on such a dour note, a figure streaks across the plaza like lightning, lightly tapping the cane in midair.
The cane changes its trajectory, falling gently into Harold's hand.
And with that, he bows once more. The show is over.
He takes in the thunderous applause.

steps.name: Depressed Passerby
steps.text: Do you think I could be like you one day, sir?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now why would you ever want to be like me, young lady? You've got two good legs, a beautiful face, and plenty of time.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You'll be even better than me, guaranteed.

steps.name: No-Longer-Depressed Passerby
steps.text: I'll try my best. Thank you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It has been a privilege to impart some courage unto a young soul such as yours, madam.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now then... How long have you been watching, Madam Degenbrecher?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I spotted you while I was enjoying a meal nearby.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You dance well.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh* Yes, well, if one is to hobnob around the upper echelons of society, one must put in some effort.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Some nobles were fond of hiding my leg for a laugh, so I put my nose to the grindstone with the help of my wife.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Nowadays, Old Harold's One-Legged Dance could be considered my calling card.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What happened to your leg?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, my prosthetic fell in the line of duty. As for why, I'm sure you can guess.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I see... It must have been of good quality to last so long.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's beyond repair?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Only one of Rhodes Island's technical experts can fix it, but Mr. Weiss doesn't feel like telling me where she is. So what other choice have I but to sigh in sorrow here in the plaza?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Are you sighing because you can't find the engineer, or because you can't get a relationship going with Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Madam Degenbrecher, you would be a most terrifying presence to encounter on a social call.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'm not interested in your parties.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: But since you have time on your hands...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Kolod.

steps.name: Bulky Youth
steps.text: What is it, ma'am?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Your dad needs men to help sow seeds this afternoon, correct?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Tell Matterhorn that this Victorian veteran will come and help.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Wait, Matterhorn... This might end up being a golden opportunity.)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Moreover, I'll have to face him down sooner or later anyhow.)

steps.name: Bulky Youth
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Are you going or not?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Of course I am.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I find I am compelled to repeat myself.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Madam Degenbrecher, you would be a most terrifying presence to encounter on a social call.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Degenbrecher said Sir Enciodes asked her for help, but she's too busy, and she sent this man instead?

steps.name: Bulky Youth
steps.text: Yep.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's been a rather long time, Mr. Matterhorn.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: I won't ask too many questions. You know your farm work?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But of course! Whenever I have the time, I head down to the fields on my land myself to help out the farmers.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Those fields might be my closest friends.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Good to hear.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, however, do wait a moment, if you could.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If it's fieldwork, this cane will just get in the way.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'd like to borrow a couple of things from you to fashion a simple leg.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: What do you need?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Some wood, a knife, some cotton, and a length of rope. Nothing too difficult.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: You can make a prosthetic out of that?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Naturally.
Matterhorn is somewhat incredulous, but Harold gets to work like he's done it a thousand times before.
He starts with a cylindrical piece of wood, measuring out the length of his missing limb, before shaving both ends of the log flat to use as his 'leg'.
Then, he finds a round, flat piece of wood, bores a hole through the middle, and inserts the 'leg' through it. And with that, he has finished his simple-as-can-be 'prosthetic'.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: I'm guessing you've made ones like those before?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Naturally.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The army gives out proper ones, of course, but battlefield conditions are fickle. If something goes wrong with yours, there's no repairing it in the middle of combat.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Times like that, a simple yet practical prosthetic such as this will suffice for marching.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Moreover, a proper prosthetic isn't cheap. Especially not for a serviceman, who will ask a lot more out of one compared to a civilian.
As he speaks, Harold carves some wood into a bowl shape, filling the inside with cotton.
He then puts the bowl flush against the wooden 'leg' and ties them together with rope, finishing it off with an incredibly tight knot.
He stands, then takes a couple of steps before making a circle. To top it all off, he bows to Matterhorn. Mission successful, it seems.
It is a somewhat comical scene, but Matterhorn can't help but applaud.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I have another one of these handmade prosthetics back at home. Whenever it's time to head down to the fields, on it goes.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: After all, the one I normally use has a terribly high price tag. Not that it's unworthy of it. It's lasted me many years, with nary a peep out of it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'd often joke with my men that if aught were to happen to me in battle, save my leg first!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's worth more than any compensation I'd get.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Do you have many fields back home?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: We do.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But not like Kjerag's. The ones at home are awash with golden wheat.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But I'd say there's still plenty the same. Wouldn't you say so, my good sir?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hnnf—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I believe that's the last of it.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: It is.
As the sun sinks into the west, Harold, Matterhorn and the farmers stand between the fields to look at the results of their afternoon's work. As one, they let out a deep breath.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Work like this always gets one puffing out the chest, eh, Matterhorn?

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: You're right. I never did expect to share a moment like this with a Victorian noble like you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha! Well, don't expect anything like that out of any others, or you'll be sorely disappointed.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: How did you become a noble, then?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A very good question.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's like how every member of the Caster family is sighing and asking why your Sir Enciodes had to be born a man of Kjerag.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: We may never have a proper answer. All we can do is treat it as a jest of fate.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Do let your master know that the next time he is in our county, he must give me a ring.

spans.text: Do let your master know that the next time he is in our county, he

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'll ask my wife to personally man the kitchen and prepare a taste of Victorian home cooking for you all.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Then you and him can stay with us a spell.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And when the time comes, we can send you off with some rousing local tunes—
Harold starts to hum softly.
The farmers by their side begin to accompany him with the folk songs of Kjerag.
Before they knew it, it had become a chorus amidst the fields, blending together songs of Victoria and Kjerag both.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Seems things are rather lively today.

steps.name: Bystander Villager
steps.text: Oh, Weiss! Delivering letters again, are we?

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: The song they're singing sounds familiar, but also a bit not, if you get me?

steps.name: Bystander Villager
steps.text: Some old Victorian's singing along with them.

steps.name: Bystander Villager
steps.text: Still sounds pretty good, though.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: An old Victorian?
Weiss follows the singing, only to find Harold counting out a beat as a local farmer sings.
His face works its way through several different expressions before finally settling on calmness.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: I could say a couple of words to Weiss on your behalf, but I can't guarantee he'll listen.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: This is just how he is. I hope you understand.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I was even more difficult to deal with when I was his age.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: It seems you won't need my help.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Wha-?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Mr. Weiss.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: If you had known that things were going to end the way they did, then why did you feel the need to keep up the pretense?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Mr. Weiss, a soldier can never in clear conscience ask his victims for forgiveness.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: All I can say is...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I really do love Kjerag.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If possible, I'd like to wish her all the best. I'm thinking of bringing my whole family here to have a look around in future.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: I just happened to pass by on the way to deliver something to that Rhodes Island engineer.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: You can come along, assuming you can keep up.
Weiss turns and walks away.
But he does not leap and bound into the distance as usual. Instead, he walks, at a speed somewhat faster than an ordinary man, heading towards the snowy mountains.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Weiss is also struggling inside.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hah! Who isn't?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm struggling too. But for me, it's more like how my stump will ache from time to time.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's not something I tell others often...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Not that anybody really cares in the first place.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Well then. Be seeing you, Matterhorn, my good man.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Hmm? Wait, Sir Harold.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: My master has just notified me that he will be holding a banquet in a few days, and he cordially extends you an invitation. Weiss, Degenbrecher and I will also be in attendance.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: So that's how it is.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Pardon?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It seems I owe a favor not just to Madam Degenbrecher, but to Sir Enciodes as well.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (I just wanted to use this opportunity to establish a rapport with Rhodes Island at first, but from the looks of things, I suppose I can even hand in my onboard application tomorrow.)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (The wandering engineer was your handiwork, wasn't it, Enciodes?)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Ah, no, can't quite say that for sure. All I can say is that we're of like mind. Me going to Rhodes Island will be a good thing for you, me, Kjerag and Caster.)

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Sir Harold?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Do tell him that I'll be bringing some top-notch liquor with me! We'll drink till we drop!
